correctness.rationale: Direct minimization expresses the loss as \(\sum_ja_jd_j\) with \(a_j=\min\{(1-\tau)P_j,\tau(1-P_j)\}\). The same gaps expand the centered support in cut indicators, yielding the strict lower bound. The cell average of the mean-zero quantile score has covariance \(a_j\) with each cut indicator, hence the whole loss equals \(\operatorname{Cov}(X,S)\); Cauchy--Schwarz gives the upper edge. Conditional variance gives the displayed closed form for \(C_\tau^2\), and the projected score has at most three levels, producing exactly the stated attainment cases. Fresh exact-rational replay verified 2500 independent profiles/levels, including the covariance identity and both bounds.

evidence: These sources are broader in the class of parent distributions and quantile identities.
They do not solve the constrained support-location extremum or supply the profile-specific variance-normalized equality cases.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Distributional representations and general quantile-location inequalities do not dominate the fixed-partition support-cone optimization.

value.rationale: Minimum pinball/check loss is the canonical unconditional quantile scale, and standard deviation is the canonical quadratic scale. The theorem completely quantifies their interaction for categorical or empirical distributions with fixed frequencies, including a transparent information-loss term when the target quantile cuts through a probability cell. This is a motivated exact profile rather than an arbitrary slice.

final_claim: For any fixed positive finite mass profile and \(0<\tau<1\), the minimized population quantile check loss divided by standard deviation has the exact profile interval with lower cut constant \(L_\tau\) and upper cell-projection norm \(C_\tau\); the lower edge is unattained for at least three atoms, while the upper edge is attained exactly for two atoms and for the three-atom case whose middle probability cell straddles \(\tau\).
limitations: Unconditional one-dimensional finite laws only; no conditional quantile-regression statement is made.
Strict support ordering controls the upper-endpoint attainment classification.
